newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower after failing to hold gains.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower after failing to hold gains.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower after the benchmark September contract failed to maintain its early move over key 78.00 cents, market sources said.
Local buying carried the contract to the high of 78.25 cents where buying interest evaporated, allowing September to ease back under the key level.
Analysts said any rally would be a selling opportunity since the technical and fundamental outlooks point to lower near term prices.
"The supply situation is holding over the market," an analyst said, referring to record crops expected from Florida and Brazil in the 1996/97 season.
The September contract closed 1.10 cents lower at 76.35 cents per lb, having traded from 78.25 to 76.00 cents. The rest of the board finished 1.30 to 1.00 lower.
Support basis the September was seen at today's low of 76.00 cents, followed by 74.05 cents.
An estimated 2,100 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 1,556 lots.
Total open interest fell by 330 lots to stand at 31,304 lots as of Thursday.
